rules.text: Cook43: masculine singular N/A stem, G -es, D -e; plural N/A -as, G -a, D -um. Retain both vowels in bisceop, ofen and æcer; their dictionary class supplies no license for arbitrary syncope.
Cook44: replace citation -e before endings; singular N/A and D have -e. Gefērscipe follows the explicitly named -scipe class.

Cook47: strong neuter singular N/A citation form, G -es, D -e; plural G -a, D -um. Heavy monosyllables have zero N/A plural. For disyllables Cook47.1 allows zero or -u; select mynstru and ēagðȳrlu. Cook47.1 explicitly selects usual wundor, not an invented plural in -as.

Cook43.4 and47.6: a short second vowel is normally lost before a vowel ending when the preceding stem syllable is heavy. Thus mynster → mynstr-, ēagðȳrel → ēagðȳrl-, wundor → wundr-. The uninflected citation form remains; do not extend syncope to ofen, æcer or bisceop.

Cook51b: long feminine singular N citation, G/D/A -e; plural N/A -a (also -e), G -a, D -um. Æx keeps æ: the single-consonant short-masculine æ/a alternation does not apply to this feminine cluster stem. Synn is the selected full citation variant of Cook syn(n).

Cook51.5: -nes doubles s before inflectional endings and retains e. Cook51.3: -ung has the ordinary feminine endings, with -a also attested in singular oblique cases; select -e consistently. Abstract plural cells are reference forms; the assigned abstract sense is singular.

Cook53: masculine N singular -a, all other singular cases and N/A plural -an; G plural -ena, D plural -um. Feminine citation -e, otherwise the same selected pattern. Productive cirican replaces citation -e; retain the source-only ciricean spelling separately.

Cook46.1 and52.2, checked against Wright415: brōðor, mōdor, dohtor have unchanged singular N/G/A; D singular brēðer, mēder, dehter. Selected N/A plural brōðor, mōdru, dohtor; G plural brōðra, mōdra, dohtra; D plural brōðrum, mōdrum, dohtrum. Dohtor has short o. Plurals brōðru, mōdra and dohtru/dohtra are documented alternatives. Wright thorn is declared normalized to Cook eth in the derived course paradigm.
Cook52.1: burg has selected G/D singular and N/A plural byrig; singular N/A burg, plural G burga and D burgum. Burge is an accepted G singular variant.

Cook46.3: frēond is the explicitly named companion of fēond. Reuse the established complete fēond model, replacing fēond-/fīend with frēond-/frīend. Selected D singular frēonde, N/A plural frīend, G plural frēonda, D plural frēondum. Do not infer genitive frēondra from the ordinary -end participle pattern.

Cook57–59: complete strong NGDA singular/plural in all three genders; masculine/neuter singular instrumental -e shown for reference. Long monosyllables lose the short-class -u in feminine N singular and neuter N/A plural. Adjectives in -e retain it only without another ending, otherwise replace it; their feminine N singular and neuter N/A plural end in -u.

Cook60: weak masculine N singular -a, feminine N singular and neuter N/A singular -e, other singular cases and plural N/A -an; G plural -ra (also -ena), D plural -um. The table establishes forms, not unrestricted article or comparison syntax.

Cook57.3 explicitly gives hālig, not hāl(i)gu, for feminine N singular and neuter N/A plural. Select syncope hālg- before vowel endings, retaining hālig- before -ne, -re, -ra. Hęfig retains its medial vowel after the light first syllable; do not create hęfges.

Cook63: regular comparative -ra and superlative -ost/-est; remove citation -e. Swētra is rule-derived from swēte; exact swētestan is independently present in the assigned source. Comparatives have weak inflection only; superlatives can use strong and weak inflection. Wright §259.3 simplifies a doubled consonant after another consonant: swētr- + -ra gives selected genitive plural swētra, not mechanically assembled swētrra. This is a rule-derived cell, not a separately attested quotation. No strong comparative table is generated.
